proposed.explanation: Your most urgent need is 10,000 EGP in cash within 3 months for a family wedding, and your total portfolio is only 5,080 EGP (1,000 EGP cash + 200 × 20.40 = 4,080 EGP in EFID). Even selling every share you own will leave you 4,920 EGP short, so you will need to find additional funds from outside this portfolio. Given that (a) your horizon is only 3 months, (b) your willingness and ability to absorb losses are both low, and (c) you need maximum liquidity, the responsible move is to sell all 200 EFID shares now and convert them to cash. This brings your cash to 5,080 EGP and eliminates any market-risk exposure over the next quarter. Although EFID's FY2025 results show strong growth (revenue up from 16.15 bn to 20.92 bn EGP; net profit up from 1.61 bn to 2.70 bn EGP; EPS doubled to 2.18 EGP), a 3-month window is too short to rely on equity appreciation, and a low-risk-tolerance investor should not gamble on a 3-month price move when a hard cash deadline is approaching. Please note that selling at 20.40 EGP is a market transaction; the actual execution price may differ slightly. You must also arrange the remaining 4,920 EGP from savings, family support, or other sources before the wedding date. This is guidance, not a guarantee; market prices can move in either direction, but the priority here is certainty of cash, not return.

claims.statement: EFID consolidated revenue for the year ended 31 December 2025 was 20,915,072,432 EGP.
EFID consolidated revenue for the year ended 31 December 2024 was 16,146,545,699 EGP.
EFID consolidated net profit for the year ended 31 December 2025 was 2,695,301,670 EGP.
EFID consolidated net profit for the year ended 31 December 2024 was 1,606,727,698 EGP.
EFID basic and diluted EPS for the year ended 31 December 2025 was 2.18 EGP.
EFID basic and diluted EPS for the year ended 31 December 2024 was 1.09 EGP.

limitations: The evidence covers only FY2025 and FY2024 annual results; there is no interim (H1 2026) data, no dividend information, no share-count detail, and no forward guidance.
The 3-month price trajectory of EFID is unknown; the 20.40 EGP price is a single-point snapshot and the actual sale price may be higher or lower.
The investor's total portfolio (5,080 EGP) is insufficient to meet the 10,000 EGP cash need; the shortfall of 4,920 EGP must be sourced externally.
No information is provided on transaction costs, bid-ask spreads, or settlement times for EFID on the Egyptian exchange.
